sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A device placed through a letterbox exploded at a home in north Belfast during the early hours. gist: Singapore threatens to prosecute companies responsible for severe Indonesian forest fires causing regional haze.
Neighbouring countries express mounting frustration as millions face school closures and respiratory illnesses.
Pressure builds on Jakarta to declare a national disaster and tackle root causes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Intense wildfires in Indonesia have caused a persistent haze to drift into neighbouring countries, including Singapore and Malaysia, affecting millions with poor air quality and school closures.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The smoke is causing respiratory illnesses, hurting businesses, and straining diplomatic relations across the region as neighbours demand accountability from Indonesia.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Singapore is exploring prosecution of responsible companies and joint regional action, while pressure grows on Jakarta to accept assistance and declare a national disaster.
